summary: Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1953–1957) and Bukkyo University (doctorate, 1991), where he served as associate professor (~1968–2005) and professor (~1978–2005).

Koji Tanaka works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Macquarie University, the University of Auckland's Department of Philosophy (attested 2011–2014), and the Australian National University's School of Philosophy.

Kojiro Yoshikawa (1904–1980) was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and president of Toho Gakkai (~1972–1980).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Sokichi Tsuda at Waseda University, where he taught as associate professor (1936) and professor (1941–1969). He also served as president of Taisho University.
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seiren Matsunami (attested 1977) and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita (b. 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960), where he later served as associate professor (~1968–1976), department chair (~1976–2002), director/professor (~1996–2002), and professor emeritus (~2002–2008).
Koki Kawagishi (1928–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.

Komal Asrani works in computational fields and Indology. After studying at Government Engineering College and earning a Ph.D. from Uttar Pradesh Rajarshi Tandon Open University (2002–2005), Asrani held a computer science post at Babu Banarasi Das Group (2006).
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Konchok Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Gottlob Anton (1745–1814) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1763–1770) and was appointed Professor of Oriental and Classical Languages at the University of Wittenberg in 1775.
Konrad Ihlefeld (1837–1906) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rostock in 1858 and served as director of Porayar Seminary from 1878 to 1885.

Konrad Klaus (b. 1956) is an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Göttingen and Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and Michael Hahn. He held deputy professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), succeeding Claus Vogel in 2001.
Konrad Meisig (b. 1953) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ulrich Schneider and held a post at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from ~1991 to 2019.

Korada Mahadeva Sastri (1921–2016) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Suniti Kumar Chatterji. He held posts at Annamalai, Sri Venkateswara, and Sri Krishnadevaraya Universities, and was a visiting professor at the University of Cologne (1976–1978).

Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) specialized in archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905) and held posts at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1909–1938).

Kosei Ishii (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa, he taught at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and Komazawa University, becoming professor emeritus (2006–2021).

Kosei Tada (1938–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Taisho University and served as president of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).
